# How a carried difference grows

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`how-a-carried-difference-grows` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](how-a-carried-difference-grows.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> The carried amount expands by order. Over all conditions and loop-free upstream a finite order is exact, growth polynomial from bounded start and inflow. With strengths in ℕ a loop multiplies it at least by one plus their product per turn; stationary, growth is polynomial only without one.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. The carried amount expands by order: order j is what routes of at most j responses carry, each order being what the strengths make of the order below, starting from the quiet levels; the carried amount carries itself. The orders rise with j, none exceeding the carried amount, and order j is exact up to step j, so the carried amount is the limit of the orders. (`Becoming.Loops.accrue`, `Becoming.carriedFrom`, `Becoming.carriedWithin`, `Becoming.carriedGive_of_part`, `Becoming.carriedGive_of_rest`, `Becoming.carriedGive_mono`, `Becoming.carriedGive_congr`, `Becoming.carriedFrom_succ`, `Becoming.carriedFrom_carried`, `Becoming.carriedFrom_mono`, `Becoming.carriedFrom_congr`, `Becoming.carriedFrom_eq_carried`, `Becoming.carriedWithin_le_carried`, `Becoming.carriedWithin_le_succ`, `Becoming.carriedWithin_mono`, `Becoming.carriedWithin_exact`, `Becoming.carried_eq_carriedWithin`)
2. The level of one condition is coupled into another where at some step a formation present, outside the part, exchanges with the second with positive strength on a level of the first up to that step; a chain of couplings leads from one condition to another, a loop back to where it started, and upstream is where a chain leads from. Where no chain of j + 1 couplings ends at a condition, order j is exact there at every step; with every condition listed, a chain as long as the list passes some condition twice, which lies on a loop upstream, so where no loop lies upstream the order one less than the number of conditions is exact at every step. (`Becoming.Loops.zero_or_pos`, `Becoming.Loops.ble_succ_self`, `Becoming.Loops.beq_self`, `Becoming.Loops.extend`, `Becoming.Loops.extend_below`, `Becoming.Loops.extend_next`, `Becoming.Couples`, `Becoming.Coupled`, `Becoming.CoupledInto`, `Becoming.OnLoop`, `Becoming.Upstream`, `Becoming.Coupled.extend`, `Becoming.coupledInto_zero`, `Becoming.CoupledInto.succ`, `Becoming.CoupledInto.shorten`, `Becoming.loop_of_coupledInto`, `Becoming.carriedWithin_exact_of_not_coupledInto`, `Becoming.carriedWithin_exact_of_no_loop`)
3. Where the couplings hold at every step, an order missing something at a condition at some step makes the next order miss something at the next step at the condition it is coupled into: along a chain the order missed rises by one per coupling, and around a loop by the loop's length every time around. So where a loop upstream carries something and a chain holding at every step leads from it to a condition, every order misses something there at some step; with every condition listed and every coupling holding at every step, some finite order is exact from every starting gap exactly where no loop lies upstream. The couplings must hold at every step: where one formation returns a condition's level to it at the first step only, the condition lies on a loop, upstream of itself, yet order one is exact at every step from every starting gap. (`Becoming.Loops.total_lt`, `Becoming.Loops.total_mul_const`, `Becoming.Loops.mul_lt_mul_of_pos`, `Becoming.Loops.le_mul_of_pos`, `Becoming.CouplesAlways`, `Becoming.CoupledAlways`, `Becoming.orderBelow`, `Becoming.carriedWithin_eq_carriedFrom`, `Becoming.orderBelow_le_carried`, `Becoming.orderBelow_mono`, `Becoming.carriedFrom_lt`, `Becoming.orderBelow_lt_succ`, `Becoming.orderBelow_lt_later`, `Becoming.orderBelow_lt_along`, `Becoming.orderBelow_lt_around`, `Becoming.carriedWithin_lt_of_loop`, `Becoming.finite_order_iff_no_loop`, `Becoming.Loops.Once.strengths`, `Becoming.Loops.Once.give_zero`, `Becoming.Loops.Once.give_succ`, `Becoming.Loops.Once.onLoop`, `Becoming.Loops.Once.exact`, `Becoming.Loops.Once.not_always`)
4. Along a chain whose couplings have strength at least w at every step, what reaches its start arrives at its end, within as many steps as it has couplings, times the product of the strengths; around a loop, what has reached it returns multiplied by at least one plus the product of the strengths around it, and after R times around by that factor to the power R. (`Becoming.Loops.mul_assoc_nat`, `Becoming.Loops.add_mul_nat`, `Becoming.Loops.mul_swap`, `Becoming.Loops.one_add_mul`, `Becoming.CoupledWith`, `Becoming.Loops.product`, `Becoming.carried_le_add`, `Becoming.carried_mono_steps`, `Becoming.carried_step_ge`, `Becoming.carried_along`, `Becoming.carried_around`, `Becoming.carried_runaway`)
5. With the part giving no gap after the start, starting gaps at most D and the strengths into each condition summing to at most M at each step: order j carries at most D times the sum over i ≤ j of the ways to place i responses among t steps times M^i, a polynomial in t of degree j; the carried amount is at most D(1 + M)^t; and a cut at order j misses at most their difference. One condition returning its level to itself with strength M, a self-loop, attains all three exactly. (`Becoming.Loops.total_steps_shift`, `Becoming.Loops.withinBound`, `Becoming.Loops.geomBound`, `Becoming.Loops.missBound`, `Becoming.Loops.withinBound_zero`, `Becoming.Loops.withinBound_le_succ`, `Becoming.Loops.withinBound_mono`, `Becoming.Loops.geomBound_mono`, `Becoming.Loops.missBound_le_succ`, `Becoming.Loops.missBound_mono`, `Becoming.Loops.missBound_add_withinBound`, `Becoming.Loops.geomBound_eq`, `Becoming.Loops.binom`, `Becoming.Loops.orderSum`, `Becoming.Loops.binom_zero`, `Becoming.Loops.orderSum_zero`, `Becoming.Loops.pow_step`, `Becoming.Loops.orderSum_succ`, `Becoming.Loops.orderSum_start`, `Becoming.Loops.orderSum_step`, `Becoming.Loops.withinBound_eq`, `Becoming.inflow`, `Becoming.total_give_le_add`, `Becoming.total_give_le_inflow`, `Becoming.carriedWithin_zero_quiet`, `Becoming.carriedWithin_le_withinBound`, `Becoming.carried_le_geomBound`, `Becoming.carried_le_carriedWithin_add`, `Becoming.Loops.SelfLoop.strengths`, `Becoming.Loops.SelfLoop.give`, `Becoming.Loops.SelfLoop.inflow_eq`, `Becoming.Loops.SelfLoop.carried_eq`, `Becoming.Loops.SelfLoop.carriedWithin_eq`, `Becoming.Loops.SelfLoop.attained`)
6. Where no loop lies upstream, the carried amount is at most a polynomial in the steps, of degree one less than the number of conditions. With the same formations and strengths at every step, every coupling holds at every step, every loop at least doubles what reaches it every time around, and what reaches a loop upstream arrives so doubled; every polynomial is outgrown by the powers of two, so the carried amount is bounded by a polynomial from every starting gap exactly where no loop lies upstream, as a finite order is exact. (`Becoming.carried_le_polynomial`, `Becoming.stationary`, `Becoming.stationary_now`, `Becoming.couplesAlways_of_stationary`, `Becoming.finite_order_iff_no_loop_stationary`, `Becoming.Loops.product_ones`, `Becoming.carried_doubles_around`, `Becoming.Loops.mul_left_comm_nat`, `Becoming.Loops.mul_mul_mul_comm_nat`, `Becoming.Loops.pow_add_nat`, `Becoming.Loops.pow_mul_nat`, `Becoming.Loops.mul_pow_nat`, `Becoming.Loops.pow_le_pow_base`, `Becoming.Loops.pow_le_pow_exp`, `Becoming.Loops.two_pow_pos`, `Becoming.Loops.two_pow_succ`, `Becoming.Loops.lt_two_pow`, `Becoming.Loops.odd_lt_two_pow`, `Becoming.Loops.sq_lt_two_pow`, `Becoming.Loops.linear_lt_two_pow`, `Becoming.Loops.poly_lt_two_pow`, `Becoming.Loops.not_poly_of_doubling`, `Becoming.Loops.binom_le_pow`, `Becoming.Loops.orderSum_le_poly`, `Becoming.inflowStationary`, `Becoming.inflow_stationary`, `Becoming.strength_of_couples`, `Becoming.carried_along_stationary`, `Becoming.carried_doubles_into`, `Becoming.polynomial_iff_no_loop`)
7. For every law of what has stood with these strengths and every two balanced flows of it: where no loop lies upstream, the most difference that can arrive is what the finite order carries, and every gap is at most the polynomial; with the same formations and strengths at every step and each condition listed once, the most difference that can arrive is bounded by a polynomial exactly where no loop lies upstream. (`Becoming.most_difference_within`, `Becoming.gap_le_polynomial`, `Becoming.gap_polynomial_iff_no_loop`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No axiom. What each theorem needs is written into it: the coupling strengths (the k of RespondsWithin) as supplied bounds; every condition listed (every); in the bounds, the part giving no gap after the start, starting gaps at most D and the strengths into each condition at most M a step; in the runaway theorems, couplings holding at every step (CouplesAlways, CoupledWith), and in the equivalences the same formations and strengths at every step (stationary); in the theorems for every law, each condition listed once (Distinct), with decided equality of conditions used only in proofs, through most_difference_arrives and gap_le_carried.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- Which strengths a given law has, or which loops a world has: the strengths enter every theorem as supplied bounds.
- That a particular law runs away around a loop: the runaway is of the most difference that can arrive, attained by the carrying law; a law exchanging nothing is within every strength and has no runaway, loop or not.
- A loop upstream does not imply that every order is inexact: a loop coupled only at some steps can leave a finite order exact; the equivalences need couplings at every step. Witness: `Becoming.Loops.Once.not_always`.
- How fast a runaway is beyond the product of the strengths around a loop; real strengths and amounts, continuous time and infinitely many conditions.
- **Counterexample:** The self-loop: one condition, whose one formation returns its current level to it with strength M, from a starting gap D; it attains the bound on a cut exactly, so no smaller bound follows from D and M. [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Loops.lean)

Readings, decided by Ren on 16 October: Ren meant Feynman diagrams, the match structural, not physical; the integration Ren asked about, for laws that are not determined, is the sum over histories with its four losses (P82, losses-of-the-sum-over-histories), and the orders here are the same structural kind, organized by number of responses as Feynman diagrams are by vertices, the two not yet joined; only a loop makes a difference run away, running away meaning faster than every polynomial, of the most difference that can arrive: only through a loop, and, with natural-number strengths, each positive one at least one, under the carrying law, through every loop that couples at every step (narrowed by the AI and taken by Ren on 18 October 2026, DELEGATED-CHOICES D43: with real strengths below one such a loop need not run away, which is damping), couplings at only some steps being open; which loops a world has is part of its situation (Ren, 16 October: “the situation makes it true”), loops forming and dissolving within the unfolding and the theorems taking them as they stand at each step, taken for now and open to revision once a loop-formation theorem exists. (After 16 October: the two are joined by orders-as-a-sum-over-histories, the orders being sums over routes back in time; the loop-formation theorem is how-loops-form, a loop forming by closing; Ren agreed on 16 October to the third reading as revised: which loops a world has is part of its situation: loops form within the unfolding by closing, a loop forming at the step at which some exchange comes to respond to a level downstream of the condition it gives to, and dissolve where their couplings stop (once the schedule has settled, a finite order is exact exactly where no loop of the couplings that go on lies upstream); where the strengths are read off the course, which loops form and when is read off the unfolding; the theorems take the loops as they stand at each step, the strengths or the way they are read being supplied.) The mathematics is standard: Picard iteration of a linear comparison system, nilpotent where the coupling graph has no cycle.

Answers the other half of Ren's question of 12 October: there, four losses of the sum over histories (a truncation misses exactly what it drops; loops double the courses); here, the carried difference expands by order, a cut misses at most a bound that is attained, and a finite order loses nothing exactly where no loop lies upstream.
- related, not a proved adapter: [what-a-cut-loses](what-a-cut-loses.md). Answers the first item of its next step, loops whose couplings come and go, for every schedule: a cut loses exactly what more responses carry, exactly where a longer chain in time order arrives; once the schedule has settled, a finite order is exact exactly where no loop of the couplings that go on lies upstream; without such a loop the growth is polynomial.
- related, not a proved adapter: [orders-as-a-sum-over-histories](orders-as-a-sum-over-histories.md). The orders are a sum over histories: the sum over routes back in time at horizon j + 1 is order j, and a cut is a truncation.
- related, not a proved adapter: [how-loops-form](how-loops-form.md). How loops form within the unfolding: through a coupling acting at the step of formation that closes a chain; before formation growth is at most polynomial.
- related, not a proved adapter: [loops-within-what-a-law-reads](loops-within-what-a-law-reads.md). Within one law: loops lie within what is read and form where reading grows; for a law reading a stock only below a threshold there is no loop through the stock before the break, and the loop forms at the break.
- related, not a proved adapter: [how-often-couplings-act](how-often-couplings-act.md). The geometric bound holds counting only the steps at which couplings act and is attained by a self-loop; in the reading Ren called right, “only a loop makes a difference run away”, couplings at only some steps are closed both ways: only a loop of the couplings that go on can make it run away, such a loop need not, and it does where its returns are frequent.
